steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat butter and white sugar together in a medium bowl until creamy. Mix in 1/2 teaspoon almond extract. Add flour and mix until dough comes together.
Form dough into 1 ½-inch balls and place on ungreased cookie sheets about 2 inches apart. Use your thumb to press down and make a dent in the center of each ball, then fill with jam.
Bake in batches the preheated oven until edges are lightly browned, about 14 to 18 minutes; allow to cool on cookie sheet for a few minutes.
Mix confectioners' sugar, milk, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon almond extract together in a medium bowl until smooth; drizzle lightly over warm cookies.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Thumbprint Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These cute raspberry thumbprint cookies, made with shortbread dough, are filled with seedless raspberry jam and topped with a sweet drizzle glaze.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make a classic version of the holiday favorite, the thumbprint cookie. Good raspberry jam is key, but drizzling the cookies with a glaze makes them amazing. Keep for yourself or give as a memorable gift.
video.name: Raspberry and Almond Shortbread Thumbprints

review.reviewBody:
These cookies taste great when made just the way the recipe is written.

But, if you're like me and your cookies always turn out flat, here's how to make these cookies turn out taller, just like the ones in the picture. First, turn the oven temp down about 10 degrees. Second, don't soften the butter before mixing, just cut it into 1 tbsp pieces and mix with the sugar. Third, add an extra 1/4 cup of flour to the dough. Finally, once you've filled the thumbprints with jam, put the whole cookie sheet in the freezer for 10 minutes before baking. The first time I followed the recipe and my cookies were so flat the jam leaked through the bottom, and the second time I made these adjustments and the cookies not only tasted delicious, they looked perfect, too!

Have been making these for Christmas since they first appeared in a Pillsbury Classic cookbook many years ago. They are a tender, buttery, melt-in-your mouth cookie that also look pretty on the plate. They do spread a bit, so I always chill the dough first and roll the dough into balls a little smaller than the recipe suggests. This is simply a perfect Christmas cookie.

Wow - a simple cooke with a absolutely decadent flavor! I mean these are really, really good. the key to these is chilling the dough, rolling them small and taking the genious advice of using a chapstick cap to make the indentions. Whoever thought of that little trick deserves a medal! These cookies definitely melt in your mouth. I used glaze featured with the recipe, but you can definitely change this up with melted white and dark chocolate - YUM!

These cookies are not only impressive, they are mouth watering delicious! I made the "thumb print" indentation with a wine bottle cork, and filled the centers with a seedless raspberry preserve that I heated on the stove for an easier consistency. I alternated the drizzle every other cookie with a semi-sweet chocolate and the almond glaze, using a zip lock baggie to pipe the glaze. This has got to be the most simple, yet impressive cookie I have ever made!

These didn't turn out exactly how I was expecting, however, the taste made up for the appearance. Make sure to space the cookies far enough apart on the cookie sheet so they don't end up molded together. AND...make your thumb print indentions deep enough so the raspberry jam doesn't run out. Mind did just that and made a mess on my cookie sheet. I suggest using your little finger instead of your thumb...so the indentions look a little more delicate. I sprinkled poppy seeds in my dough before baking to give the cookies a little "something". I had to use a little more than 1 tsp of milk to make a glaze. I poured my glaze into a ziploc bag, cut off a corner and drizzled the glaze on the cookies. Again, despite the runny jam, these did taste really good and I do recommened them:) Thanks for sharing Dee. P.S. The second batch I made, I used the top of a chap-stick container to make my indentions...they turned out great!!

I love these cookies. I chilled them overnight and baked them today. I found that putting the jam in a ziploc bag to pipe helped keep from making a mess and made the jam easier to handle--squishing it in the bag warms it up. I think they look adorable and they taste delicious! *Update*: I made these once with the hand mixer. I won't ever do that again! It makes the butter melt and they don't turn out. Use a pastry cutter like I usually do and they will turn out very well.

I make these every once in a while, and they’re always received with praise. They’re so easy to make but I always forget the little tips modifications I make to them. I think about half the sugar (or just less than what the recipe calls for) balances out much better since the raspberry jam is already sweet enough. I use 1/4 tsp of almond extract and 1 tsp of vanilla extract as the almond can come through too strongly for my taste. Add flour a little at a time as sometimes I still have a little bit of flour left over when dough meets my preferred consistency, and I kneed with my hands as it becomes too thick for my kitchen aid after half the flour goes in. After dough is spread out on baking sheet and center has been pressed in, place into freezer for about 10 mins so it holds its shape while baking. Lastly, the raspberry jam can be spooned into a small sandwich bag with one corner tip cut off to make it easier and quicker by piping into center of cookies. I hope this helps!

I've been making these cookies for years and just made them again this weekend! For those having trouble with spreading, you need more flour and/or more space between cookies. I can only do one dozen at a time in my convection oven. Try baking one or two cookies first to make sure the cookies aren't spreading too much. You should be able to roll the dough into a log shape on your counter without leaving behind sticky bits of dough. You'll need more flour on a humid day because of the moisture in the air. If you find the glaze hard to apply, you can paint it on the cookies with a pastry brush or just dust the cookies with powdered sugar instead.

I made these last year (2023) at Christmas time. While the cookies tasted delicious, I had same experience as others, they came out flat and the same as others commented, had questioned whether it was missing an ingredient. Fast forward to 2024, I did some research (my husband loves these cookies, so I was determined to find the ‘fix’). The recipe IS missing an ingredient. I added a 1/4 teaspoon of salt and refrigerated them on cookie tray for 1 hour prior to baking and they came out perfect! They retained their shape nicely, no splitting. Other modifications I made were to use unsalted butter and I rolled each cookie ball in ground almonds. To make the ‘thumbprint’, I used the back of my 1/2-teaspoon measuring spoon, which made perfect indents.

Context: I’m an open-the-bag, break-and-bake kind of cookie baker, so I was surprised at how well I was able to make these fussy-looking cookies (anything that is easy but looks impressive is what I’m looking for). This is a fantastic recipe for what I wanted, but there are some challenges with it: 1) the dough balls are a bit difficult to form because the dough is rather grainy using softened instead of melted butter - if you don’t like handling PlayDoh, I’d pick a different recipe - so I used a disher/ice cream scoop for size consistency and warmed the dough slightly in my hands to get it to form up. 2) pressing your thumb into a ball of dough causes not only dough to go up under your fingernail (ew) but also makes some weird impressions and cracks on the outside edge of the cookie that I don’t like, so I formed them into 1/2” thick patties instead of balls used a melon baller to get a satisfyingly perfect circle indention that would hold a good amount of preserves. 3) spoons + preserves + me is not a good equation for accuracy so I used snipped storage bags to pipe in those preserves that come in the fancy jars at the store - I made strawberry and blackberry (overfilling will make you sad). 4) the amount of almond extract the recipe calls for in the glaze was overwhelming so I use 1/4 tsp vanilla and a little milk instead. Much more balanced that way and doesn’t overshadow the excellence of the preserves! Move over Pillsbury, these are now my husband’s favorite cookies!

I thought this recipe turned out great. I made some of the adjustments I read from different comments: 
1. I added the jam halfway through baking. Another poster suggested piping the jam into the imprint by using the baggie method - brilliant!
2. I froze the dough for about 15 mins after placing on the cooking sheet and making the imprint.
3. The icing needed more than a teaspoon of milk...I used about 1.5 teaspoons, plus the almond extract.
I forgot to add the extra 1/4 cup of flour. My cookies spread slightly, but I think adding a tad extra flour will make these flawless.

It was very good, and I liked the glaze thing, although some people who tried it thought it was too sweet. if you don't like sweet things, I would either change the glaze or forget it entirely. also, I think that it works better with more bitter jam. if you aren't sure, try different jams, and put the glaze on maybe half? overall, it was amazing, would make it again.

I have used this recipe as a base to start with. I have made these raspberry thumbprints but I have also changed the jam flavors and I have used orange and lemon curd too! The extract changes depending on the filling too...enjoy!

Made these twice per recipe thus far.. Made dough the night before/ used beater to cream butter and sugar but when I added the flour I used my hands to mix and form a nice ball of dough.l then rolled into balls/ put on cookie sheet without preserves and refrigerated over nite. Took out in the morn and let stand on counter while I filled w preserve and then popped into the oven. These are the best shortbread jam cookies and super easy to make . I did substitute vanilla for almond. Not a big almond fan. I got a little "nutty" and "sparingly" sprinkled finely crushed walnuts on top of each cookie. Yummy for sure! Our go to shortbread cookie now!

I like a little larger cookie and used a 2tbs scoop. I found that after scooping, roll the dough into a smooth ball before placing it in the pan and flatten slightly. This helps keep cracking to a minimum. Take time to enlarge the well made by your thumb. I used blackberry jam for filling and added a touch of lemon extract to the icing. The icing did need a touch more milk to pipe.

I have used this recipe for YEARS and my family loves it! Whenever I share the cookies with anyone, they ask for the recipe. I have made this several times, and I've never had them come out any way other than perfect. I'm not sure why some people have had problems with them spreading or turning out flat. The flavor and texture are wonderful! This is my favorite cookie!
No changes. Great recipe! Thanks

The cookie has good flavor and texture, but they came out really flat. I'm thinking that more flour or less butter is needed. I would either tweak the recipe or go with another one. (I filled some with strawberry preserves and homemade lemon curd instead of raspberry preserves.)
I should have the read the reviews first. Waste of ingredients. Totally flat
Cookies were pretty decent. We made them bigger as just the two of us devouring them ;) I added extra glaze to them also. Placed on my Mi mitten platter and let them cool a bit.
